post_title: What annualized real GDP growth will the BEA report in its advance estimate for Q3 2026, released October 29, 2026?

question.title: What annualized real GDP growth will the BEA report in its advance estimate for Q3 2026, released October 29, 2026?
question.description:
The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) publishes quarterly estimates of real gross domestic product (GDP) growth, expressed as a percent change at a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR). For each quarter BEA issues three successive estimates (advance, second, third); the advance estimate is the first and is based on incomplete source data, so it is often revised. The advance estimate for the third quarter of 2026 (July–September) is scheduled for release on October 29, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET, per the BEA release schedule (https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule).

Recent readings: real GDP rose 2.5% in Q1 2026 (revised) and 2.2% in Q2 2026 (third estimate). As of October 15, 2026, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model nowcast for Q3 2026 was 3.6% (https://www.atlantafed.org/research-and-data/data/gdpnow), down from 3.7% earlier in the month. GDPNow tends to run higher than BEA's eventual advance print. The Philadelphia Fed's Survey of Professional Forecasters third-quarter 2026 median for Q3 real GDP growth was 2.5%. A FY2026 federal government shutdown in late 2025 previously delayed and in some cases cancelled economic data releases, but the Q3 2026 GDP advance estimate remains on the published schedule for October 29, 2026.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the percent change in real gross domestic product (GDP) at a seasonally adjusted annual rate for the third quarter of 2026, as stated in the "GDP (Advance Estimate), 3rd Quarter 2026" news release published by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on October 29, 2026. The figure is the headline "Real GDP" percent change (SAAR) reported in that release (available via the BEA release schedule at https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule and linked from https://www.bea.gov/ ). For example, a reported increase of 2.8 percent resolves as 2.8, and a decrease of 0.5 percent resolves as -0.5.
question.fine_print: Resolution uses the advance (first) estimate only; subsequent second and third estimates do not affect resolution. If BEA reschedules the advance estimate release to a later date (e.g., due to a government shutdown or administrative delay), resolution waits for that release and uses the first published advance estimate of Q3 2026 real GDP growth. If the BEA page is unavailable, the figure as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) citing the BEA release will be used.
